summary: DNS flip to secondary edge during pin-refresh causes intermittent cross-region egress and spikes in EU p95
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Health, enterprise) reported intermittent latency spikes and occasional 429s beginning during a control-plane maintenance window. Symptoms suggest some requests from eu-west tenants are briefly routed through a US-based secondary edge after a pin-refresh event. Impact: production traffic for several EU regions saw p50 and p95 increases ~30-160ms and elevated 429 counts for short windows.

Impact:
- Increased request latency (p50 +40–80ms, p95 +120–180ms) for eu-west for 3 short windows on 2026-03-12.
- Burst of 429s observed correlated to the same windows.
- Customer reports higher than expected egress hops and cross-region tracebacks in logs.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API, prod (eu-west primary), tenant pinned to eu-west strict residency.
- Affected workloads: low-latency chat endpoints, token-length ~512.

Observed at: 2026-03-12 03:12Z, 2026-03-12 11:47Z, 2026-03-12 21:05Z

Expected behavior:
- Pin-refresh should maintain eu-west egress and DNS should not flip to a us-east edge for strict-residency tenants.

Notes: customer flagged this after seeing TLS endpoint in traces resolving to us-east edge IPs during the windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use enterprise account with strict residency pin to eu-west.
2) Send steady stream of requests to chat-generation endpoint (token length ~512) from eu-west client endpoints.
3) Trigger pin-refresh by toggling a temporary control-plane flag (simulated in staging) or observe during maintenance window in prod.
4) Observe DNS resolution order and traceroute from client side, monitor p50/p95 and 429 counts in the Redwood Console.
5) Check TLS peer IPs in request traces to confirm any us-east egress hops.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 04:00Z - Maya Patel: Initial triage, correlating spike windows with control-plane maintenance logs. Noted DNS entries for tenant were TTL=30 during refresh windows.

2026-03-12 05:30Z - Diego Ramos: Pulled edge healthcheck logs; primary eu-west edge reported transient control-plane disconnects lasting ~6-12s during each window. Secondary-edge announced itself as healthy and was selected by global DNS for some lookups.

2026-03-12 08:10Z - Diego Ramos: Found that pin-refresh sequence briefly clears the per-tenant DNS sticky record, exposing resolver to region-priority ordering which favors a fallback edge (us-east) when eu-west edge healthcheck had short flakiness.

2026-03-12 12:15Z - SRE: Verified that resolver caches on customer side had low TTLs; combined with control-plane refresh this allowed some clients to re-resolve to fallback. This explains mixed resolved_ip entries in traces.

2026-03-12 13:45Z - Networking: Observed increased SYN retransmits to eu-west during those seconds consistent with backend transient load spike; autoscaler responded but initial probe failures caused edge selection flip.

2026-03-13 09:22Z - Diego Ramos: Reproduced in staging by lowering eu-west edge health threshold and triggering a pin-refresh: DNS responses during the refresh included both eu-west and us-east IPs; some clients preferred us-east leading to higher RTT.
comments: 2026-03-12 06:02 - Priya Nair (Acme Health): We're seeing user-facing latency alerts and a handful of 429s. Can you confirm this is not data leaving EU for logging? We need assurance about data residency compliance.

2026-03-12 06:20 - Maya Patel (Support): We're investigating. Short answer: metadata indicates requests still handled by Redwood and logs show only edge location differences. We'll confirm no customer data left account boundaries and produce a timeline.

2026-03-12 09:00 - Diego Ramos (SRE): Internal note: control-plane refresh sequence can clear sticky DNS targeting for ~5–15s. Working on mitigation: ensure DNS answers prefer same-region edges for pinned tenants during refresh window.
2026-03-13 10:00 - Priya Nair (Acme Health): Appreciate the update. Can you provide a temporary mitigation until a permanent fix is in place?

2026-03-13 10:15 - Maya Patel (Support): Proposed workaround: set pin-refresh window to low-traffic hours and temporarily increase per-tenant DNS TTL to 60s to reduce re-resolves. Engineering to validate side effects.
2026-03-14 08:30 - Diego Ramos (SRE): Rolling a canary of DNS preference tweak to ensure eu-west A records are prioritized for pinned tenants during refresh. Monitoring for error regression.
resolution: Workaround applied: increased per-tenant DNS TTL on Acme Health to 60s and temporarily delayed non-critical pin-refreshes until maintenance windows with low traffic. Root cause: control-plane pin-refresh logic cleared sticky DNS entries while eu-west edge experienced brief health-check flaps, allowing global DNS to hand out fallback us-east addresses. Mitigation path: implement control-plane change to preserve region-priority answers for strict-residency tenants during refresh windows and harden edge healthchecks to avoid brief flaps. Engineering has opened infra PR to prefer same-region edge IPs for pinned tenants and added additional healthcheck smoothing. Follow-up: schedule postmortem and formal change rollout (related PR linked).
follow_up_actions: Create postmortem and share with Acme Health (owner: Maya Patel) - due 2026-03-20
Merge DNS preference patch (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1842) and run canary in eu-west - owner: Diego Ramos
Add automated test in staging to simulate pin-refresh + edge flake and assert no cross-region answers - owner: SRE team
Confirm compliance: provide Acme Health export of TLS peer IPs during windows and sign-off that no logs left outside tenant's legal boundaries - owner: Compliance
Consider making DNS TTL configurable per tenant for enterprise customers - product ticket to follow.
